\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Product Differentiation}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.ProductDifferentiation
\section{Overview}
Gaussian product densities and their first mean derivatives have common local integrable envelopes. Differentiation under the integral gives continuously differentiable bounded Gaussian averages and a uniform derivative norm bound.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Common scalar density and derivative envelope]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_two_derivatives_dominated}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_meanDerivative_dominated,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPDFReal_secondMeanDerivative_dominated,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianPDFReal_mean}
\difficulty{5}
For $v>0$ and $M\ge0$, let $p_v(m,z)$ be the Gaussian density with mean $m$ and variance $v$. There exists a nonnegative Lebesgue-integrable $b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that $p_v(m,z)\le b(z)$, $|((z-m)/v)p_v(m,z)|\le b(z)$, and $|((z-m)^2/v^2-1/v)p_v(m,z)|\le b(z)$ whenever $|m|\le M$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Mean derivative of a Gaussian product density]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative}
\leanok
Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. Let $A_v(c,z)$ be the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_i\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$. The product-density derivative is $A_v(c,z)$ for mean and input vectors $c,z\in\mathbb R^I$.
\end{definition}

\end{lemma}
